scope: The generic average uses the existing regular unitary group and strong operator integral; bicommutant membership is inherited from the actual generated core. Strong convergence uses the fundamental theorem of calculus on vectors, not assumed operator norm continuity.

The norm and Fourier evaluation retain the h>0 premise and the original dual Haar normalization. Plancherel yields integral of the squared dual orbit =2pi/h times norm(v)^2, hence dualQuadraticIntegral=norm(v)^2/h.
The actual normalized regular Fock vacuum gives weight(averageSquare(1))=1. This supplies a nonzero finite positive input; the infinite unit is not passed off as finite.
The finite-square left ideal is closed under left multiplication and strongly dense by A*average(h) as h approaches zero from above. This statement is not a claim of norm density or trace cyclicity.
Order normality invokes the existing internal directed-supremum theorem on positive elements of the same core. No equality of this dual-invariant weight to the exp(-s) scaled trace is asserted.
